The tab shows the next run. Works with the server running or stopped; "Keep the newest N" removes old ones; a backup that is already running or a busy server (update, install ...) skips that minute. Runs missed while NodeGSM was closed are not made up. Results appear in the NGSM log as normal `server:backup` events.

changelog.title: 2026-11-25 - Discord bot: per-user per-server permission rules
items: **Why:** not every Discord user should be able to run slash commands or manage every installed server. Authorisation is now a list of rules `<discordUserId> <serverId> <action,action,...>` (new setting `settings.discord.permissions`, a list of `{ userId, serverId, actions[] }`).

**Rules:** `serverId` is a numeric server id, or `0` / `*` for all servers. Actions: `check list start stop restart update send backup stats`, plus the shortcuts `all` (every action; `send` still needs **Allow raw commands**) and `read` (check, list, stats). Case and spaces around commas are tolerated; `#` comments; rules for the same user + server are merged; a user's rules for one server and for 0 are a union.

**Semantics:** default deny. Server actions need a rule for that server or for 0. `check`, `list`, `stats` are global: any rule listing them is enough; `/list` and `/stats` then show only servers the user has any permission for (all with a server-0 rule). Server autocomplete offers only servers the user may use for that command. Admin roles keep full rights. The deprecated `allowedUserIds` list behaves exactly as before (all commands) and the rules are additive. The per-server `discordAllowedUserIds` narrowing applies to legacy users only; rules are authoritative for their user. No rules + no legacy ids + no admin role = nobody.

**Denials:** ephemeral and specific ("You do not have permission to use /restart on server 4.", never the rule list); the `discord:command` event log entry gets `required` (the action) and the server id (`serverId`); successful entries get `via` (`admin` / `rule` / `legacy`).

**Code:** new `services/discordPermissions.js` (parse, format, strict sanitise, match; no I/O); `discordCommands.js` `authorize()` / new `authorizeAction()`; `settings.js` sanitises `discord.permissions` (digit-only ids 15-25 long, known actions only, server id 0..999999999, at most 500 rules, merged). The bot reads the rules live (no reconnect; they are not part of the connection signature). Slash-command registration JSON unchanged.
**IPC:** `discordPermParse(text)` (rules + per-line errors + unknown-server warnings + server names) and `discordPermFormat(rules)`; `saveSettings` carries `discord.permissions`.

**UI:** Discord > Bot > "Permissions per user and server": textarea, help and examples, live validation (errors block saving, unknown servers warn), preview table (user, servers by name, actions). The old "Allowed user IDs" box is marked deprecated; the "nobody is allowed" warning now also counts rules.

**Not verified:** nothing was tried against real Discord. See [docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md](docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md) (the "zero for all" wording was interpreted as server id 0 = all servers; please confirm).

**Docs:** [docs/GUIDE-discord.md](docs/GUIDE-discord.md) (new permissions section), README, TECH-architecture, TECH-api, TESTING-CHECKLIST, OPEN-QUESTIONS. **Tests:** parser (valid / invalid lines, `*` and 0, all / read, case and spaces, dedupe / merge, cap), settings sanitising, authorisation matrix (server-specific, 0 = all, action not listed, send gate, list / stats / autocomplete filtering, admin, legacy unchanged, narrowing, empty = deny, live read), event log detail, no reconnect on change, registration JSON unchanged, IPC.

changelog.title: 2026-11-24 - Web mode and Linux support (headless server)
items: **Headless web server:** `npm run serve` (also the `nodegsm` bin entry) starts `src/server/headless.js`: Node `http` + the `ws` package (pinned 8.23.0), no Electron. It serves `src/renderer` and `assets/` as static files and mounts the same API table as the IPC on `POST /api/<channel>` (`{ "args": [] }` -> `{ ok, data }` / `{ ok: false, error }`); the push events (`status`, `console`, `consoleOut`, `logLines`, `removed`, `metrics`, `cluster:progress`, `discordBot`) arrive over `WebSocket /ws`. Binds `127.0.0.1:8730` by default (`--host`, `--port`, `--data`, env `NODEGSM_*`). SIGINT / SIGTERM stop the game servers through the same shutdown path as quitting the desktop app.

**Security:** authentication is required. Token from `NODEGSM_TOKEN` or generated on first start into `<data>/web-token` (0600, printed once); login page (`login.html` + `login.js`, no inline scripts) and a signed in-memory session cookie (`HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`, `Secure` behind HTTPS); bearer token for scripts; constant-time compare; failed logins rate limited per client address (429); Origin must equal Host for cookie requests (CSRF), JSON content type only, request body limit, no CORS; strict path confinement for static files and `GET /download/backup`; `GET /healthz` unauthenticated and returns only `{ "ok": true }`; a non-loopback bind without authentication is refused. No TLS built in - use a reverse proxy; tokens are never logged.

**Core extracted:** `src/main/core.js` (`createCore`) holds everything that used to be wired in `main.js` (data folder contents, settings, plugins, ServerManager, services, MetricsCollector, scheduler start / stop, push-event hub). `main.js` (Electron) and the headless server both use it; Electron behaviour is unchanged. Electron-only ctx members get headless stand-ins (folder picker / open folder / relaunch report "not available in web mode").

**Renderer in both modes:** `transport-web.js` defines `window.wgsm = { call, on, mode }` over fetch + WebSocket (auto-reconnect with backoff, redirect to the login page on 401) and does nothing inside Electron. New `platformInfo` channel (`mode`, `platform`, `features`); desktop-only controls carry the class `desktop-only` and are hidden in web mode; backups get a **Download** button; links open in a new tab; Import accepts a typed path.

**Linux platform layer** (`src/main/platform.js`): process-group `SIGTERM` / `SIGKILL` instead of `taskkill`, CPU / RAM / threads from `/proc`, `taskset` affinity, SteamCMD from `steamcmd_linux.tar.gz` (`steamcmd.sh`, same arguments, `+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType` when a step asks for another platform), GNU `tar` extraction, `chmod +x` before start, XDG data folder, firewall "not managed" message with a `ufw` hint. `serverManager.js`, `metrics.js`, `steamcmd.js`, `installRunner.js` call it; Windows behaviour is unchanged (the existing tests pass unchanged). **Only unit-tested; never run on real Linux.**

**Plugins:** optional `platforms` (default Windows only), `run.linux`, `run.env`, `install.linux`, steamcmd step `platform`; validated, in the JSON Schema and in `registry.json`. The game browser and Add Server show a "not available on this platform" badge and creation / import is refused. `mc`, `csgo`, `rust` and `palworld` now declare Linux support (**declared, untested**); no other plugin was changed.

changelog.title: 2026-11-24 - Clusters: update, config sync, clear folders

Create needs at least 2 servers, **all the same game**, the parent must be a member, a server can be in **one** cluster only. Rename / set parent / add / remove members / delete (servers are never deleted). When a server is removed it leaves its cluster (`mgr 'removed'`); a deleted parent is replaced by the first remaining member; fewer than 2 servers dissolve the cluster (logged).

**Cluster update:** updates the parent through `mgr.update(id, validate, { cluster })` (plugin `update.validateArgs` applies), then copies the parent's files to every member **without overwriting** plugin config files (`configs[].path` and `.bak`), `cluster.preserve`, the cluster's own preserve rules and `configs/wgsm.json`. `onlyChanged` skips files with identical size + mtime (copies keep the parent's mtime). Members are processed one after another, running ones are stopped first and restarted afterwards; progress is pushed as `cluster:progress` (`phase`, `percent`, `memberId`, `memberName`, `memberIndex`, `memberCount`, `message`). Dry-run `clusterUpdatePlan` returns counts, sizes and the preserve list per member. A member without the file gets the parent's copy with a `protected key not present in member` warning. `clusterConfigPlan` returns a unified-style diff per member and file (nothing written), `clusterConfigApply` writes with a `.bak` and logs (`cluster:config-sync`, plus `server:config`).

**Events / log:** `cluster:created`, `cluster:deleted`, `cluster:update-started`, `cluster:update-finished`, `cluster:update-failed`, `cluster:config-synced`, `cluster:cleared` on `mgr.events` (payload `{ id: parentId, name, game, ts, detail }`); NGSM log entries `cluster:*` (see the guide).

**IPC:** `clusters`, `clusterCreate`, `clusterSave`, `clusterDelete`, `clusterUpdatePlan`, `clusterUpdate`, `clusterConfigPlan`, `clusterConfigApply`, `clusterClearPlan`, `clusterClear`; push event `cluster:progress`.

Both themes.

changelog.title: 2026-11-24 - Backups: full/neat pick, restore, restore as new, backup list
items: **`services/backup.js`** (`BackupService`, also reachable as `mgr.bk()`): modes `full` (whole server folder) and `neatpick` (plugin `backup.presets` ids + chosen relative folders/files, optionally the server's `wgsm.json`). Exclude patterns = plugin `backup.exclude` + user patterns (`*`, `**`, `?`; no `/` = match by name anywhere, with `/` = from the server root). `ServerManager.backup / backupList / restore / deleteBackup` now delegate to it (same names; bulk backup, backup-on-start and old backups keep working).

**Streaming zip** (`services/zip.js`, no new dependency): files are read, deflated and written chunk by chunk, zip64 when needed, written to `*.partial` and renamed when complete; the reader extracts entry by entry with CRC and size checks. AdmZip is no longer used for backups.

**Manifest** `backup-<ISO>.json` next to every zip (`version, mode, game, serverName, serverId, createdAt, paths, presets, exclude, sizeBytes, uncompressedBytes, fileCount, gameVersion, includesServerSettings, skipped?, missing?`); backups without one are treated as `full`. **Safety:** all selection paths are normalised (no `..`, absolute paths, drive letters or `:`), symlinks / junctions are never followed, and every zip entry name is validated before anything is extracted (zip-slip), including through links already in the server folder. Locked files are skipped and counted.

**Restore:** Full extracts over the files (server stopped first); Neat pick requires an installed server ("install the game first, then restore"); a backup of another game is refused; `restoreSettings` optionally re-applies the saved `wgsm.json`. **Restore as new server** (`restoreAsNew`) creates a new server from the manifest's game (Full: extract; Neat pick: run the install, then apply), applies the saved settings except `id / game / installDir`, moves a taken port to the next free one, removes the new server again on failure and reports a missing plugin clearly. Old backups without a manifest need `game`.

**Events:** `server:backup` detail now has `mode, sizeBytes, fileCount, skipped`; `server:restore` has `mode, fileCount` and, for restore-as-new, `asNew, from`. Extra NGSM log entries `backup:pruned / backup:skipped / backup:failed / backup:restore-failed` (the event log registers itself as `mgr.eventLog`).

**IPC:** `backups()` = all backups of all servers (server name, game, `deleted`, `legacy`, manifest), `backups(folder)`, `backup(id, opts)`, `backupInfo(id)` (presets, plugin excludes, retention), `backupPreview(id, opts)`, `restore(id, file, opts)`, `restoreNew(folder, file, opts)`, `deleteBackup`, `backupDownload(folder, file)` (reveals the zip), `backupOpenFolder(folder)`.

changelog.title: 2026-11-24 - Foundation for clusters, Discord and backups
items: **`src/main/api.js`:** the IPC `handle()` table moved out of `main.js` into `buildApi(ctx)` (`{ name: fn }`); `main.js` mounts it on `ipcMain` with the same channel names and `{ ok, data }` / `{ ok: false, error }` wrapping. No behaviour change; a web transport can mount the same table later.

**Event bus:** `ServerManager.events` (EventEmitter) emits `server:started | stopped | crashed | restarted | updated | backup | restore | command` with `{ id, name, game, ts, detail }`. The existing Discord `alert()` calls are unchanged.
**Service skeletons** in `src/main/services/` (`eventLog`, `discord`, `discordBot`, `backup`, `cluster`, `autoClear`): constructed and started/stopped from `main.js`, no behaviour yet.

**New settings keys** (validated in `settings.js`): `ui` (panel collapse flags), `headerStats` (cpu, ram, disk, servers, players, tick), `discord` (webhook, bot token, application/guild id, allowed user ids, admin role ids, `allowRawCommands`, per-event toggles) and `logging.retentionDays`. Nested patches merge key-wise. Note: the bot token is stored as plain text in `settings.json`.

**Optional plugin fields** (all backward compatible): `cluster`, `configs[].protect`, `backup`, `events`, `logging`, `consoles`, `update.validateArgs`, `files.autoClear`. Added to `plugin.schema.json`, validation (relative paths without `..`, regexes compile, ids unique), `toGame()`, `registry.json` (only when present), `plugins/_template` and PLUGINS.md.
**Fixed:** a console command written while a server was being stopped could raise an unhandled `EPIPE` on the process stdin; stdin errors are now ignored.

**Tests:** new fields accepted/rejected, settings sanitising of the new keys, `server:*` events from a fake server (start, command, stop, backup, restore, kill, crash), API table and service skeletons.

changelog.title: 2026-11-24 - Dashboard, server table and bulk actions
items: **Views:** header switch *List / Table / Dashboard* (last view remembered). **Table** is the horizontal WindowsGSM-style list with checkboxes; **Dashboard** shows system CPU/memory/disk, server counts, active players, a 30-minute history chart (players / CPU / memory) and the running-server table.
**Multi-select bulk actions:** Start, Stop, Restart, Kill, Update, Backup on any number of selected servers (new `kill` = force-stop the whole process tree; `bulk` runner with per-server results).

**Column picker** in Settings (also on the Table toolbar and Dashboard): ID, PID, icon, status, name, game, IP, port, query port, map, players, CPU, memory, uptime, threads, restarts + plugin metrics. One list for Table and Dashboard; reset to default.
**Plugin `metrics`** (FPS, tick rate, entities ...): regex on console or a declared log, optional console command polled on a timer; validated, in the schema and template.

**Fixed:** PID / CPU / memory stayed empty for servers without a query port (the first Started event fired before the process existed); deleting a server no longer leaves its backups for a new server that reuses the id (they are moved aside as `<id>.deleted-<time>`).
**Tests:** process-tree totals, collector (CPU/memory/threads, console + command + log metrics, history), bulk start/stop/kill/backup incl. skipped and unknown actions, settings sanitising.

changelog.title: 2026-11-24 - Themes, settings and documentation links

changelog.title: 2026-11-24 - Website
items: **New `website/`**: futuristic dark-mode static site (Home, Features & changelog, Plugins, Download). Layout inspired by the WindowsGSM site, written from scratch.

**Plugins page** with forgiving search (fixed: "7daytodie" / "7 days to die" now find 7 Days to Die; matches names, ids, abbreviations, tags, app ids and small typos, ranked by relevance), tag filter, sort, per-plugin drawer (details, README, official/unofficial docs, how to install), zip download, star rating, comments and a Markdown **community info** page anyone can edit (revision history).
